component.name: Reelix
component.summary: Record your screen, natively on GNOME
Graba tu pantalla de forma nativa en GNOME

description.p: Reelix is a lightweight, local-first screen recorder built for GNOME and Wayland. It uses the XDG Desktop Portal and PipeWire to capture your screen or a single window, together with your microphone and system audio, and GStreamer to encode MP4 files, with hardware acceleration when available.
Your recordings never leave your computer. There is no account, no cloud and no telemetry.

description.p: Low resource usage: the camera bubble is processed on the GPU (about a third of the CPU it used), and a maximum recording resolution setting.
New icon, RPM and Flatpak packages, and a more robust pause that works with every capture source.
Much smaller files (no container padding), GPU encoding and colour conversion on Intel, and recording statistics.
Pause and resume without gaps, countdown before recording, a recordings library (rename, show in folder, copy, details, move to trash), preferences and optional system-wide shortcuts.
Floating camera bubble with a live preview and a colour-shifting border, recorded as part of the screen; recording controls on the bubble.
Phase 3: overlay the webcam on the recording as a rectangle or a circle, in any corner, in three sizes.
Phase 2: record the microphone and system audio (mixed, with a level meter and a limiter) into the MP4 as AAC.
Phase 1 proof of concept: record a screen or window to MP4 through the ScreenCast portal.
